finding.title: A retry overwrites a file that is never overwritten
finding.wrong_outcome: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a writer that never overwrites (`Existing files in the output directory are never overwritten; a numeric suffix is added to the new file name.`, S:7) and a retry that overwrites the partial file (`the retry reuses the file name of the failed attempt and overwrites the partial file`, S:12). The retry must add a suffix and reuse the name, so the retry test cannot pass.

e1.text: Existing files in the output directory are never overwritten; a numeric suffix is added to the new file name.
e1.context:
R1. Exports are written to the directory named by the --out option.
R2. If --out is not given, exports are written to the exports folder in the current working directory.
R3. The service creates the output directory if it does not exist.
R4. Existing files in the output directory are never overwritten; a numeric suffix is added to the new file name.

## 2. File names
R5. A file name has the form report-YYYYMMDD-NNN.csv, where NNN is a counter starting at 001.

e2.text: the retry reuses the file name of the failed attempt and overwrites the partial file
e2.context:
## 2. File names
R5. A file name has the form report-YYYYMMDD-NNN.csv, where NNN is a counter starting at 001.
R6. The counter resets to 001 at midnight UTC.
R7. When an export is retried, the retry reuses the file name of the failed attempt and overwrites the partial file.

## 3. Formats
R8. The default format is CSV with a header row.
